text: [1] Power (measured in kW) expresses the rate at which energy is consumed or produced, while energy (measured in kWh) refers to the total amount of energy consumed or produced over a period of time. kW and kWh are not interchangeable because kW is a rate (power) and kWh is a unit of energy, which depends on both power and time. For instance, a 100 W appliance running for three hours consumes 300 Wh or 0.3 kWh, showing that energy is power multiplied by time. [1]
